problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+16y=9\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$

Find the general solution to this equation given that the complementary solution is ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{-4x},$ where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

$y(x)=A{e}^{-4x}\,+\,($
{{field-1}}
$)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)\,+\,($
{{field-2}}
$)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)$
worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

To find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
4\frac{\text{d}{y}_{c}}{\text{d}x}+16{y}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving this equation, we find that the complementary solution is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{-4x}
$$

where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $9\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-4\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+4\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
4(-4\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+4\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x))+16(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(4x))=9\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(16\alpha +16\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+(-16\alpha +16\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)=9\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}16\alpha +16\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)) \\ -16\alpha +16\beta =9\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x))\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{9}{32},\beta =\frac{9}{32}.$

Therefore, 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{9}{32}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+\frac{9}{32}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{-4x}+(-\frac{9}{32})\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+(\frac{9}{32})\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x).
$$
